newsitem.title: USA: FCC chair dismayed by early reviews of TV ratings.
newsitem.headline: FCC chair dismayed by early reviews of TV ratings.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission said Friday he was "disappointed" the television industry's proposed system for rating programmes has failed to generate more public approval.

"I am frankly disappointed that it is not immediately playing to rave reviews," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt told a press conference. "The early critical remarks are significant," Hundt added, although for now he is reserving any judgment.

The FCC is in a position to approve or reject the age-based ratings, to be formally unveiled next week. "Obviously, from my perspective, life is easier if everybody in the audience says: 'What a great show,'" Hundt said.
Some lawmakers, educators, children's advocates and parents' groups loudly complain that the TV industry's motion-picture-style plan does not offer parents enough information.
They want a content-based system specifying the level of sex, violence and strong language.
The planned ratings -- such as "TV-K7" for children older than seven and "TV-M" for mature audiences -- are meant to show what programmes are suitable for kids of different ages.
Hundt said he will withhold judgment until the FCC has studied the new system and issued it for public comment.
"This is a case where I haven't seen the movie and I haven't even seen the preview. I'm glad that they've volunteered something," Hundt said of the TV industry group developing the ratings.
Under this year's telecommunications law, the FCC must set up an advisory panel to craft a ratings system if the industry fails within a year to draft an "acceptable" plan.
But a spokesman for the TV industry group made clear Thursday it would use only its plan and would fight in the courts on First Amendment grounds any government-imposed system.
